exercise.name: Dumbbell Step-down

reference.title: Dumbbell Step Down (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Dumbbell, step, exercise type Strength

exercise.laterality: Unilateral (the leg on the box works)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you stand back up.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, light tap, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: Higher box, slower lowering, then heavier dumbbells. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Stand on the box near its front edge, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.
Shift your weight onto the right foot and lift the left foot just off the box.
Breathe in and bend the right knee slowly; the left foot reaches forward and down. Right knee stays over the middle of the foot.
Lightly touch the left heel to the floor; do not put weight on it.
Breathe out and straighten the right leg to stand tall; bring the left foot back onto the box.
Stand tall on both feet and reset; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.fix: Keep the knee over the 2nd-3rd toe; lower the box if it keeps happening.
Control the whole lowering; only tap the heel.

mistakes.mistake: Hip hiking or the pelvis dropping
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips level and the trunk tall.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing off the floor with the free foot
mistakes.fix: The leg on the box does all the work.

kinematics.norm: Deepest at the heel tap; set by the box height and leg length; Lewis 2015 compared tasks at 60 degrees and at peak knee flexion
More hip adduction and less knee abduction than in a single-leg squat (Lewis 2015); keep the knee over the foot
Slight forward lean; trunk flexion was the only difference between the 16 and 24 cm steps at 60 degrees of knee flexion (Lewis 2015)
Heel touches the floor in front of the box without taking weight (clinical opinion)
Slow lowering, 2-3 s; about 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1173712, Dumbbell Step Down (male), video (movement reference)
Lewis, Foch, Luko, Loverro & Khuu 2015, differences in lower extremity and trunk kinematics between single leg squat and step down tasks (PLoS ONE 10(5):e0126258)
Hip-muscle activation during the lunge, single-leg squat, and step-up-and-over exercises (J Sport Rehabil 18(1):91-103, 2009; PubMed 19321909)
MacAskill, Durant & Wallace 2014, gluteal muscle activity during weightbearing and non-weightbearing exercise (Int J Sports Phys Ther 9(7):907-914)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a stable box that cannot slide; stand near its front edge only when you can control the lowering.
modify: Knee pain: lower box (15-20 cm) and a shorter lowering.
Balance concerns: one dumbbell, free hand on a rail or wall.

muscleNotes.quads_r: The knee extensors of the leg on the box lower the body slowly (eccentric) and straighten it again (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: The knee extensors of the leg on the box lower the body slowly (eccentric) and straighten it again (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor of the standing leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor of the standing leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Holds the pelvis level on one leg: compared with a single-leg squat, step-downs showed more hip adduction and more pelvic drop on the free side (Lewis 2015).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the pelvis level on one leg: compared with a single-leg squat, step-downs showed more hip adduction and more pelvic drop on the free side (Lewis 2015).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Co-contract around the standing knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Co-contract around the standing knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the standing shin as the knee travels forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the standing shin as the knee travels forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Stop the pelvis dropping toward the free leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Stop the pelvis dropping toward the free leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright as it tips slightly forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright as it tips slightly forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders level and stop the dumbbells pulling the shoulder blades down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders level and stop the dumbbells pulling the shoulder blades down (clinical opinion).
